newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ disappointed at latest U.S. dairy subsidies.
newsitem.headline: NZ disappointed at latest U.S. dairy subsidies.

text.p: New Zealand's International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith said on Wednesday he was disappointed the United States was to carry out a further round of export subsidies under its Dairy Export Incentive Programme.
The subsidies, potentially worth millions of dollars a year, are designed to assist the competitiveness of U.S. dairy exports in selected international markets.
The subsidies are applied to designated amounts of produce.
"New Zealand has already protested to the U.S. on a number of occasions about the subsidies," Smith said in a statement.
He said the use of the scheme again this year was disappointing in view of the early moves being made by the U.S. to seek liberalisaed trade accords with New Zealand, among other countries.

"The U.S. is well aware of our concerns on this score. But I had hoped that, in the spirit of commitments made by the U.S. to a freer international trading environment, the Americans might have moved by now to end these subsidies."
Smith said New Zealand would be monitoring closely the practical impact on New Zealand dairy exports of the latest subsidy allocations.
"It is the unsubsidised New Zealand producer who bears the brunt of subsidisation by others," he said.
"I will be taking every opportunity to remind countries which maintain such unfair practices that New Zealand takes a dim view of such selectivity when it comes to trade liberalisation."
